question: Who among the following was a Roman Catholic missionary who worked in Bengal for the majority of his/her life?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mother Teresa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mother Teresa, officially known as Saint Teresa of Calcutta, was a Roman Catholic missionary who worked in Bengal, particularly in Kolkata (formerly known as Calcutta), for the majority of her life.
 
• She dedicated her life to serving the poor, sick, and marginalized people in Kolkata, establishing the Missionaries of Charity and receiving worldwide recognition for her humanitarian work.
 
• Mother Teresa, originally named Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu, was born on August 26, 1910, in Skopje, now North Macedonia.
 
• She joined the Sisters of Loreto at the age of 18 and moved to Ireland to train as a missionary.
 
• In 1929, Mother Teresa arrived in Kolkata (formerly Calcutta), India, where she taught at St. Mary's School for girls.
 
• During a train ride to Darjeeling in 1946, she experienced what she referred to as a "call within a call" from God to work among the poorest of the poor.
 
• In 1950, Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity, a Roman Catholic religious congregation dedicated to serving the destitute and dying.
 
• The Missionaries of Charity focused on providing care, shelter, and support to the sick, homeless, orphans, lepers, and individuals dying on the streets of Kolkata.
 
• Mother Teresa's selfless and dedicated service to the poor and marginalized garnered global attention, and the Missionaries of Charity expanded internationally.
 
• She received numerous awards and honors for her humanitarian work, including the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.
